headline: Apple revamps Siri AI with conversational and personalized features
summary: The revamped Siri, powered by Google's Gemini, integrates with your messages, photos, and emails for a more helpful experience, rolling out with iOS 27.
details: Apple's long-awaited Siri AI overhaul is finally here, integrated into iOS 27. This new version is designed to be conversational, omnipresent, and genuinely helpful, feeling drastically different from its predecessors.

The AI assistant is now deeply personalized, leveraging your messages, photos, and emails to understand your needs better. It also boasts improved app interaction and more natural language understanding, moving beyond simple web link suggestions.

Powered by Google's Gemini models through Apple Intelligence, the new Siri offers concise, bite-sized responses. It can also scan your device data for easy reference, though initial indexing may take over a week.
Privacy is a key focus, with Apple's Private Cloud Compute ensuring user data is not stored and only accessed when Siri is actively queried. Users can opt out of Siri AI features in their settings.

Compatibility varies: iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, all iPhone 16 and 17 models, and the iPhone 17 Air, 17 Pro, and 17 Max will support the new Siri AI, with some models offering more advanced voice options.

headline_marked: Lithuanian startup launches [[open-source drone detection network]]
headline: Lithuanian startup launches open-source drone detection network
summary: A new system uses volunteers' Android phones to listen for the distinct engine sounds of Shahed-type drones, creating a real-time acoustic map.
details: A Lithuanian startup, Mainline, has partnered with activists to create an open-source drone detection system called Drone Radar. The initiative leverages unused Android smartphones from volunteers to continuously analyze ambient sounds for the specific low-frequency signatures of Shahed-type drones.

Verified volunteers power up an old smartphone, place it near a window, and run a dedicated app. This app analyzes sounds in real-time, and if a suspicious signature is detected, it's cross-referenced with data from nearby devices to pinpoint the drone's potential location.

The project aims to build a large-scale civic acoustic detection network, with a goal of recruiting 10,000 active users across the Baltic states and Poland. The system is designed to identify drones and their locations using minimal data, prioritizing user privacy.

The Drone Radar initiative includes a public map displaying detected drone sounds and a sensor app for participants. The team is also exploring integrating audio from surveillance cameras and potentially installing sensors on mobile network towers.

The project is supported by experts from the Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Association, the Baltic Institute of Technology, and members of the Lithuanian Riflemen's Union, highlighting a collaborative effort between technology, security, and civil society.
